messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High p95 latency spike detected across inference nodes (eu-west-1). Auto-page sent to on-call.
Alex Chen: seeing p95 jump from ~120ms -> ~900ms for redwood-large-v1 in eu-west-1. Traffic still routed there. Any idea if this is infra or model-level?
Jordan Reyes: I’m on it — paging in. grabbing recent logs now.
Maya Patel: also seeing increased retry rates and a few 504s in the fronting LB. 10% of requests failing for some tenants.
Jordan Reyes: confirmed. CPU utilization on a subset of worker pods is normal but GPU compute stall metrics show long kernel waits. attaching sample log below.
Jordan Reyes: ```
[2026-03-15T09:12:23Z] worker-53 kernel-wait 0.42s
[2026-03-15T09:12:24Z] worker-53 kvcache-miss spike
[2026-03-15T09:12:25Z] worker-53 emit: output-delay 0.98s
```
Kelly O'Neill: could be NVLink saturation or PCIe hiccup on a node group. Last infra change was kernel driver update 3h ago? @infra
Jordan Reyes: rolling quick health check on node group eu-gpu-pool-3. If it's hardware, we'll want to drain and fail over.
Maya Patel: ops-sre charts show a coincident spike in inter-node RMA errors ~09:11.
sre-bot: Alert correlated: network retransmits increased 4x on eu-gpu-pool-3 between 09:10-09:14.
Alex Chen: mitigation plan options:
- A) Reroute new requests in eu-west to dedicated fallback cluster in eu-fallback (warm, lower cost model variant)
- B) Throttle concurrent per-tenant to reduce queuing
- C) Drain affected nodes and let autoscaler replace them
- D) Temporary quality degrade: switch requests to quantized redwood-small-v1 for best-effort latency
Jordan Reyes: priority is to reduce customer-facing error/latency. I propose A + B as immediate, C in parallel.
Priya Singh: agree — do A first. If we route traffic, we should update status page and CS. I'll draft messages.
Jordan Reyes: executing reroute policy now: switching routing policy for eu-west to prefer eu-fallback-cluster (lower throughput but healthy). Applying per-route throttle: max_concurrency=12 per-tenant for impacted routes.
Jordan Reyes: applied. Observability: p95 dropped to ~260ms after reroute, 5m ago.
Alex Chen: good. let's keep throttles for 30m and monitor for any errors from fallback cluster.
Maya Patel: watching errors — 504s dropping to near-zero. keep an eye on throughput impact for heavy customers.
Priya Singh: DRAFT public status update (short):
```text
We are investigating an elevated latency and errors affecting inference requests in the EU (eu-west-1). Traffic has been routed to a healthy fallback cluster to mitigate user impact. We continue to monitor and will provide an update within 30 minutes. No action required by customers at this time.
```
Priya Singh: DRAFT customer notification for impacted tenants (CS template):
```text
Hi <Customer>,
We detected elevated inference latency and intermittent errors in our EU region starting at 09:10 UTC. We have routed traffic to a healthy fallback cluster and implemented temporary throttles to stabilize service. You may see slightly higher latency or reduced throughput during the mitigation window. We will follow up with a root cause and ETA for full recovery.
Apologies for the disruption — Priya on the CS team is available if you need a direct update.
``` 
Priya Singh: sending that to CS channel and will post brief public update on status.redwood.ai/status
Sam Ortiz: flagged top 5 impacted accounts and emailed them a proactive note. they asked for ETA and if any data loss — none expected.
Alex Chen: customer impact assessment (quick):
- Scope: All inference requests to redwood-large-v1 in eu-west-1 routed through standard pools. ~12% of EU traffic affected during spike window.
- Severity: degraded latency and transient errors, best-effort mitigated via reroute.
- Risk: temporarily reduced throughput for very high QPS tenants due to throttle.
Jordan Reyes: initiating node drain for eu-gpu-pool-3 now; autoscaler will provision replacements. ETA for node replacement ~12-18 minutes per node.
Kelly O'Neill: infra note: rolling kernel driver rollback is an option but risky mid-incident. prefer node replacement and deeper postmortem.
Alex Chen: timeline & ETA to recovery:
- 09:10 UTC: first spike detected
- 09:18 UTC: reroute + throttles applied (mitigation active)
- 09:25 UTC: p95 trending down to 260ms
- Estimated full recovery (all nodes replaced & routing normalized): 45-90 minutes
Jordan Reyes: handing off on-call at 09:30 UTC to Kelly O'Neill. Handoff summary below.
Jordan Reyes: HANDOFF -> Kelly O'Neill: actions completed: reroute to eu-fallback-cluster, throttle applied, node drain started on eu-gpu-pool-3. Follow-ups: monitor replacement nodes, validate kernel driver on replaced nodes, coordinate with infra for potential driver rollback if replacements still show RMA errors.
Kelly O'Neill: ack, taking. I'll keep the incident channel active and coordinate with infra. Will update status page in 15m with progress.
Alex Chen: internal comms snippet for ops also (to paste in internal status):
```text
Incident: EU inference latency spike (eu-west-1)
Impact: Elevated p95 and intermittent 504s for redwood-large-v1; ~12% EU traffic affected.
Mitigation: Rerouted requests to eu-fallback-cluster; applied per-tenant concurrency throttles; draining affected nodes for replacement.
Next steps: node replacement, infra kernel verification, rollback decision if replacements not stable.
Owner: Kelly O'Neill (on-call)
ETA: 45-90m
``` 
Priya Singh: posted public status and sent customer emails. logged replies from two enterprise customers asking for 1:1 — routed to Sam.
Sam Ortiz: handling comms with those two; they'll want an impact timeline and whether SLA credits apply. I'll collect logs and link once we have RCA.
Maya Patel: metrics look stable for the fallback cluster. No new errors in last 4 minutes.
Jordan Reyes: note: I collected kernel/drivers and RMA logs and pushed to /reports/incidents/1934567890 on our internal bucket.
Kelly O'Neill: thanks. I'll monitor replacements and will post another public update at 09:45 UTC or earlier if we normalize.
Alex Chen: thanks everyone — leaving channel but ping me if we need to escalate to infra on-call or if rollback becomes necessary.
incident-bot: NOTE: on-call handoff recorded. New owner: Kelly O'Neill at 09:30 UTC.
Kelly O'Neill: quick checklist for handoff to next shift: 1) ensure all replaced nodes pass nvlink/PCIe self-test; 2) remove routing preference after 1h stable; 3) lift per-tenant throttles gradually.
Priya Singh: will prepare a follow-up customer update once we confirm normalization.
Kelly O'Neill: UPDATE 09:45 UTC: p95 at 170ms, error rate within normal bounds. continuing node replacements but traffic will stay on fallback for 30 more minutes to be safe.
Alex Chen: great recovery trajectory. please open postmortem draft and include timeline, kernel driver versions, and decision rationale for reroute vs rollback.
Kelly O'Neill: will do. closing handoff notes here; keep monitoring channel active until final normalization.
